finding: 195 of 240 criteria (81%) have no span of their own. Striking any one of them removes text that also earns other criteria, so the segmentation does not deliver the strike mechanic it exists for. The 20 apstats-frq-u12-* items are worst: 10 criteria each across only 6-8 spans, so every criterion shares.
evidence: Mean over-strike fraction (struck text not exclusive to the criterion) is 0.82 across all 240 criteria; for the 195 it is 1.00 -- every character struck is shared. Example, apstats-frq-u12-001: 10 criteria, 4 content spans, one per response part. Striking part-d-criterion-03 ("Explains why a histogram would be inappropriate") strikes the whole (d) paragraph, removing the text earning part-d-criterion-01 and -02. The builder self-disclosed this as open question B-005 and correctly noted in SUMMARY.md that the "removing any one criterion never empties the answer" invariant is satisfied only by the uncredited "Response:" span and does not imply criterion-level strike behaviour.
recommended_action: Re-segment before Open Hand ingests these. The fix is mechanical, not a re-authoring: the shared spans are multi-sentence and their sentences already map one-to-one onto the criteria, so splitting at sentence boundaries closes it with full_text unchanged. Note the work order's own invariant table has no "each criterion has exclusive text" row -- add one, or this recurs in work order G across 221 FRQ.

finding: derivations[] is complete in count but not re-derivable as specified. `inputs` carries a boilerplate {label: "stored item source"} plus a stem quote rather than the operands, and `expression` repeats the entire answer sentence for every value it contains. The work order called this field "the single most important field for QA on this task, because it is what lets a second model re-derive your arithmetic instead of taking it on trust."
evidence: 331 derivations across 46 items. For APSTAT-MOD3-H001-INV the five values 29, 2.045, 44.8, 805.2 and 894.8 all carry the same `expression` (the full sentence) and the same `inputs` quote. Looked-up critical values are also mis-kinded: 2.045 (t*, df 29) and 1.2816 (z, 90th percentile) are tagged kind="computed" though they come from a table, and their `inputs` quote does not source them.
recommended_action: No content change needed -- QA re-derived everything by reading. Tighten the schema for work order G: `inputs` must carry the operands as name/value pairs, `expression` must be the formula for that one value, and table lookups should be kind="looked_up" with the distribution and parameters named.

finding: The builder self-declares (open question B-004) that the authoring protocol prefers a non-OpenAI author where an OpenAI model will grade later, and that the sanctioned external route could not be used because transmitting the packet was not authorised in that environment. All 46 answers were therefore authored by Codex locally.
evidence: open_questions.csv B-004, disposition: "Completed local Codex authorship as the explicitly assigned work order and require independent cross-model QA before approval."
recommended_action: Product Owner decision, not a QA call. The work order did assign Codex the authorship and DECISION-0052 names Codex as drafter, so this is not a breach -- but it touches the DECISION-0045 gold-set lane boundary and should be confirmed rather than assumed. These answers must not be used as gold-set evidence.

finding: Statistical correctness is excellent. All 55 distinct computed derivations were independently re-derived and every one is correct, including the chi-square, both Welch t-tests with their Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, the binomial and normal-approximation work, and every two-way table whose margins reconcile.
evidence: Spot checks: chi-square 52.21 on df 2 from expected counts (124,76,124,76,62,38) recomputes to 52.207; Welch t = (68-72)/sqrt(36/25+25/25) = -2.561 with df 46.5 (reported -2.56, "about 47"); sigma = sqrt(200*0.06*0.94) = 3.3586 (reported 3.359); Var(Y) = 8,000,000 - 400^2 = 7,840,000, SD = 2,800. Also 0 orphan numbers among 618 numeric tokens in the answers, and 0 occurrences of second-person rubric phrasing.
recommended_action: No action. Record as the counter-example to work order A's authoring problem: B's authored spans score a mean word-level similarity of 0.167 against their own learner_facing_text with zero at or above 0.70, versus A's 0.582 with 15 at or above 0.85. B wrote answers; A largely echoed the rubric.
